title: Prepare for the Worst. And start saving cash now... (Here's why)
creator: Akshat Shrivastava
summary: Akshat Shrivastava makes the case for holding at least 20% cash (he holds 20–25%) in Indian and US portfolios, and why not 50%. His $1 million portfolio is up about 68% in dollar terms in roughly 1.5 years (now about $1.2 million). On the US, valuations are stretched — forward P/E about 21, Nasdaq about 26, top quartile — but index earnings growth of 15–17% is expected, so he favours profit-booking over exiting; markets have seen four 15–20% pullbacks in 2.5 years, and cash lets you rotate in. Going 50% cash risks missing run-ups from all-time highs, whose cost exceeds a 20% drawdown. On India, P/E about 18 gives valuation comfort but growth is the problem: no AI engine, and about 80% of India's AI investment comes from US firms such as Amazon and Meta, which will siphon profits; the market is flat over three years, about −15% in USD terms, and sits at a pivotal support, the next 6–7% lower — he waits for confirmation before deploying. With US rates near 5% and UAE deposits near 6%, he suggests parking cash in short/medium bonds at 5–6%, or, for advanced investors, writing puts for 8–10% yield. Most macro positives are already priced in, so a negative surprise is likelier; on Meta he notes it hit his target near its ~$850 all-time high and he is trimming some, with little margin of safety left in most US stocks. No explicit calls — no BUY/SELL/HOLD on any Indian ticker, no ₹ levels stated.
